stack.name: Domain
stack.line: Own the name and anchor the identity.
stack.detail: The domain is the one piece of your presence you fully own. Your site, your email, your profiles, and the references other people make all point back to it.

stack.name: Website
stack.line: Build the destination the business controls.
stack.detail: Profiles and marketplaces change their rules. A fast, well-structured site on your own domain is where people land, what search engines index, and where AI systems find your own account of who you are.

stack.name: Search
stack.line: Become technically sound, relevant, and discoverable.
stack.detail: Crawlable, fast pages organized around what people actually search for, plus the local and technical signals that help the right page appear.

stack.name: Entity
stack.line: Establish who you are and how everything relates.
stack.detail: Your website, founders, services, locations, profiles, reviews, and references, described consistently and connected in structured data, so systems can tell you apart from everyone with a similar name.

stack.name: AI
stack.line: Become easier for AI systems to understand, verify, cite, and surface.
stack.detail: AI-powered search and assistants draw on the same evidence: your pages, your entity signals, and what credible sources say about you. Stronger evidence leaves them less to guess.

stackReinforce: The layers reinforce each other. A strong site on a confusing name is harder to trust. Search work on a site with no structure has little to stand on. AI systems lean on all of it at once.

intro: A good-looking site can still be invisible. Most of the problems we see are structural: pages that do not match what people search for, slow templates, duplicate URLs, missing structured data, and content no one can find from the home page.
We fix that at the foundation. Information architecture comes before visual design, and the technical work is built in from the first template, not added after launch.

work.title: LuckyDomains.io: off Wix, onto a site the company owns
work.summary: The company site moved from Wix to a hand-built static site on GitHub Pages, with the duplicate-URL problems fixed and every decision written down in a public repository.
work.problem: The old site ran on Wix. It was small and dated, and it carried a recurring subscription for capability the business was not using. The owner wanted a site that was portable, versioned, and editable by coding agents.
work.approach: Rebuild as plain static HTML with no framework and no build step, served from GitHub Pages on the company's own domain. Fix duplicate URLs with canonical tags and consistent internal links, because a static host cannot write server redirects.
done: Moved the site from Wix to GitHub Pages on the apex domain, with HTTPS
Rewrote 93 internal links to one canonical form
Gave every page a self-referencing canonical tag that matches the sitemap
Kept old .html addresses as noindex stubs that point to the new URLs
Shared one Person identifier for the founder with kenashe.ai
Added a dependency-free test suite that runs on every push
lessons: On a static host, canonical tags and consistent internal links do the job redirects cannot.
Blocking duplicate URLs in robots.txt backfires: a blocked page cannot be crawled, so its canonical tag is never read.
Writing decisions down makes the next change faster, whether a person or an agent makes it.
work.noMetrics: No traffic, ranking, or lead figures are claimed for this project.
work.built: Built and deployed with an AI agent, with the decisions recorded in the repository.

work.title: One identity across two sites
work.summary: Ken Ashe's Person data uses one stable identifier on both kenashe.ai and luckydomains.io, with 19 profile references and four professional credentials described in structured data.

Then the homepage: the one place a business tells its own story, on its own terms.
Search turned the web into ranked answers. Structure and relevance decided who appeared.
Search engines began organizing facts about people and companies, not just pages.
Now AI systems summarize and recommend. They lean on every layer that came before.

Decision D11: old .html addresses stay as small noindex pages that point to the new URL, because a static host cannot redirect.
